title: Storage
summary: Storing goods properly protects quality and prevents spoilage.

sections.heading: Chilled goods
items: No wooden, cardboard or paper containers.
Use plastic or stainless steel containers.
Everything covered, with its lid or at least cling film.

sections.heading: Frozen goods
items: The same container rules as chilled goods.

sections.heading: Other storerooms
items: Bottle crates: kept apart, so they don't bring pesticides or rodenticides from their original storage.
Wine: locked, to prevent unauthorized consumption.
Cleaning products: separate from food, to avoid chemical contamination.

sections.heading: FIFO and spoilage
paragraphs: Spoilage is the loss of raw materials, semi-finished or finished products that went bad, almost always because food safety rules weren't followed. Following them protects the customer's health and your wallet too.
When counting inventory, rotate the stock: first in, first out (FIFO). Keep the oldest items within reach.
